  • How to Write an SOP
  • Affordable Countries for BD Students

FAQ

How long does the visa interview take?
Usually 3–7 minutes. The officer has already reviewed your file before you sit down.

What should I do if I don't understand a question?
Politely ask the officer to repeat it. Better than guessing.

Can I reapply if rejected?
Yes, but only after addressing the rejection reason. Reapplying without changes almost always fails again.

item.title: CGPA to Percentage Conversion — Complete Guide for BD Students
item.author: Study Koro
item.description: Why there is no single official CGPA-to-percentage formula in Bangladesh, the formulas commonly used, and what to put on your CV or job application.
item.content:encoded:
One of the most common questions on Bangladeshi student forums is: "What is my CGPA in percentage?" The honest answer is that there is no single official conversion formula, and using the wrong one on a job application or study-abroad form can make you look either dishonest or unprepared.

This guide explains how the conversion actually works in Bangladesh, the most commonly accepted formulas, and when you should — and shouldn't — convert.

Why there is no single official formula

Bangladesh's University Grants Commission (UGC) defines the 4.00 GPA scale, but it does not publish a percentage-conversion formula. Each university and each ministry uses its own:

  • Most public universities issue transcripts that already include a "percentage of marks" column alongside the CGPA — that is the authoritative number for that university.
  • Private universities sometimes only issue CGPA. They will provide a percentage on request.
  • The Ministry of Public Administration uses one formula for BCS eligibility; WES (used for North American university applications) uses another.

If you are filling a job, scholarship, or visa form, use the percentage printed on your transcript wherever possible. Only fall back to a formula when no transcript value exists.

The three commonly used formulas

1. The 10 × CGPA formula (used by some Indian universities, not standard in Bangladesh)

Percentage = CGPA × 10

So a 3.5 CGPA = 35%. This is obviously wrong for the Bangladeshi 4.00 scale and should never be used. It only makes sense in systems with a 10.00 CGPA scale.

2. The 25 × CGPA formula (a rough approximation)

Percentage = CGPA × 25

This puts a 4.00 CGPA at 100% and a 3.00 at 75%. It's the formula most commonly used by students online, but it inflates the percentage for high CGPAs and is rarely accepted by official bodies.

3. The grade-cutoff method (most accurate)

Map each course's grade back to the midpoint of its marks range, then average. Because the UGC scale defines:

  • A+ (4.00) = 80–100 (midpoint 90)
  • A (3.75) = 75–79 (midpoint 77)
  • A− (3.50) = 70–74 (midpoint 72)
  • B+ (3.25) = 65–69 (midpoint 67)
  • B (3.00) = 60–64 (midpoint 62)
  • B− (2.75) = 55–59 (midpoint 57)
  • C+ (2.50) = 50–54 (midpoint 52)
  • C (2.25) = 45–49 (midpoint 47)
  • D (2.00) = 40–44 (midpoint 42)

You weight the midpoint by credits, the same way you compute CGPA. This produces a percentage that closely matches what most Bangladeshi universities print on transcripts.

Quick reference table

CGPA Letter Approx. Percentage UK Classification
4.00 A+ 85–100% First Class
3.75 A 75–79% First Class
3.50 A− 70–74% First Class
3.25 B+ 65–69% Upper Second (2:1)
3.00 B 60–64% Upper Second (2:1)
2.75 B− 55–59% Lower Second (2:2)
2.50 C+ 50–54% Lower Second (2:2)
2.25 C 45–49% Third Class
2.00 D 40–44% Pass

For specific use cases

BCS and government jobs

The Bangladesh Public Service Commission (BPSC) explicitly converts CGPA using a fixed chart in its circular. The cutoffs for eligibility (e.g. "first division equivalent") are defined there. Always download the latest circular instead of using a generic formula.

Study abroad — US universities

WES (World Education Services) re-evaluates your transcript using its own internal methodology. You don't convert; WES does it for you, and the WES report is what universities trust.

Study abroad — UK universities

UK universities map your CGPA directly to their classification system (First, 2:1, 2:2). Use the table above as a rough guide, but check each university's "international qualifications" page for Bangladesh.

Study abroad — Australia and Canada

Most institutions accept your transcript's percentage column. If your transcript only shows CGPA, contact admissions and ask which conversion they use.

What to write on a CV or job application

  • Write "CGPA: 3.65 / 4.00" — always include the scale.
  • Don't convert to percentage unless the form specifically asks for one.
  • If a Bangladeshi employer asks for "marks," quote the percentage from your transcript, not a self-computed one.

Tools that help

Our University CGPA Calculator uses the UGC grade-point values directly and shows your CGPA on the 4.00 scale. Combine it with the table above for percentage estimates.

Related reading

  • How GPA is Calculated in Bangladesh
  • How to Improve Your CGPA in 1 Semester
  • Complete Study Abroad Guide

FAQ

Is CGPA × 25 the official conversion?
No. It's a commonly used approximation but is not endorsed by UGC. Use your transcript's percentage column whenever possible.

How do US universities convert my CGPA?
They typically don't — they use WES or a similar credential evaluator, which uses its own internal methodology.

What CGPA is equivalent to a First Class?
Approximately 3.50 and above on the 4.00 scale, though some employers set the cutoff at 3.00.

item.title: How to Write a Statement of Purpose (SOP) — With Examples
item.author: Study Koro
item.description: A clear structure for writing a strong SOP, with a worked example and the most common mistakes Bangladeshi students make.
item.content:encoded:
Your Statement of Purpose (SOP) is the single most important document in your study-abroad application after your transcripts. Admissions committees read thousands of them, and most are forgettable — generic openings, recycled clichés, and long paragraphs about how "passionate" the applicant is. A good SOP does the opposite: it tells a focused story about why this programme, at this university, is the logical next step in your career.

This guide walks Bangladeshi students through what an SOP actually is, the structure that works for most programmes, and includes a worked example you can adapt.

What an SOP is — and isn't

An SOP is a 700–1,200 word essay (one to two pages) that answers three questions:

  1. Why do you want to study this specific subject?
  2. Why this university and this programme?
  3. What will you do with the degree afterwards?

It is not a CV in paragraph form, not a list of your achievements, and not an emotional plea. Admissions officers already have your CV and transcripts. The SOP is your chance to connect the dots between them.

Structure that works

1. Opening (1 short paragraph)

Skip the quote, the dictionary definition, and the "ever since I was a child" opening. Start with a specific moment, project, or problem that made you interested in the field. One paragraph. Concrete.

2. Academic background (1–2 paragraphs)

Walk through your undergraduate degree — what you studied, the courses or projects most relevant to your target programme, and your final-year thesis or capstone. If your CGPA is strong, mention it; if it's weak in early semesters but improved later, briefly acknowledge the trajectory.

3. Professional or research experience (1–2 paragraphs)

Internships, jobs, freelance projects, research assistantships, published papers — whatever applies. Don't list responsibilities. Describe the problem you worked on, what you did, and what you learned. Numbers help: "improved processing time by 35%" beats "worked on optimisation."

4. Why this programme (1 paragraph)

This is where most Bangladeshi students lose points. Don't copy-paste the university's website. Name two or three specific things: a faculty member whose research aligns with yours, a particular course or specialisation track, a research lab or industry partnership. Show you've actually read the programme page.

5. Career goals (1 paragraph)

Short-term goal (first 2–3 years after graduation) and long-term goal (5–10 years). Tie them back to Bangladesh if relevant — universities and scholarship committees love applicants who plan to contribute to their home country.

6. Closing (2–3 sentences)

Brief, confident, no fluff. Reaffirm why the programme is the right fit.

Worked example (opening paragraphs)

"During my third-year project at BUET, I built a low-cost air-quality sensor network for three intersections in Dhaka. The data we collected over three months showed PM2.5 levels averaging 187 µg/m³ — more than seven times the WHO guideline. That project taught me two things: the public-health cost of unmanaged urban data in Bangladesh is enormous, and the technical tools to fix it are within reach. It is this combination — applied data engineering for public-sector problems — that I want to pursue in the MSc in Data Science for Public Policy at the University of Edinburgh."

Notice what this opening does: specific project, specific number, specific programme. No clichés, no childhood story, no "I have always been passionate about technology."

Common mistakes Bangladeshi students make

  • Overly formal language. "It is with great enthusiasm that I hereby submit my application…" — cut it. Write the way an educated professional speaks.
  • Listing achievements instead of explaining them. An SOP is not a CV.
  • Generic "why this university" paragraphs. Switch the university name and 90% of SOPs still make sense. That's a failure.
  • Talking about family struggles for sympathy. Only mention personal background if it directly explains a gap in your record or genuinely shaped your academic interest.
  • Bengali-to-English translation issues. Get a fluent speaker to proofread. Better yet, two.

SOP length and formatting

  • 700–1,200 words unless the university specifies otherwise. Check the application portal carefully — some have strict word or character limits.
  • 11–12 pt font, single or 1.15 spacing, normal margins.
  • No headings unless the application specifically asks for them.
  • One file, PDF, named clearly: SOP_FullName_University.pdf.

Tailor every SOP

If you are applying to 6 universities, you need 6 SOPs. The first 70% can be the same — your background, projects, and career goals don't change. The "why this programme" section must be rewritten every single time. This is the most common reason strong applicants get rejected from their top choices.

Related reading

  • How to Study Abroad from Bangladesh — Complete Guide
  • Student Visa Interview: Common Questions
  • IELTS Preparation Tips for Band 7+

FAQ

How long should my SOP be?
700–1,200 words for most programmes. Always follow the university's instructions if they specify.

Should I mention my CGPA?
Only if it strengthens your case, or if you need to explain a low semester. Use our CGPA Calculator to confirm the number you're quoting.

Can I use the same SOP for multiple universities?
No. The programme-specific section must be rewritten for each one.

item.title: How GPA is Calculated in Bangladesh (SSC, HSC, University)
item.author: Study Koro
item.description: Step-by-step explanation of how SSC, HSC, and university CGPA are calculated in Bangladesh, including the 4th-subject rule and the UGC 4.00 scale.
item.content:encoded:
"What's your GPA?" is one of the most common questions a Bangladeshi student hears — from teachers, parents, university admission officers, and employers. But surprisingly few students can actually explain how the number is calculated. SSC, HSC, and university CGPA each use slightly different rules, and getting them mixed up leads to wrong predictions, wrong applications, and wrong scholarship calculations.

This guide explains exactly how GPA is calculated at every level of education in Bangladesh, using the official rules of the Ministry of Education and the University Grants Commission (UGC).

SSC GPA — how it works

SSC (Secondary School Certificate) is graded on a 5.00 scale by all general education boards (Dhaka, Chattogram, Rajshahi, Khulna, Barishal, Sylhet, Jashore, Comilla, Dinajpur, Mymensingh) and Madrasah and Technical boards.

Marks-to-grade conversion

Marks Letter Grade Grade Point
80–100 A+ 5.00
70–79 A 4.00
60–69 A− 3.50
50–59 B 3.00
40–49 C 2.00
33–39 D 1.00
0–32 F 0.00 (Fail)

How the GPA is averaged

SSC GPA is the simple average of grade points of the main subjects (excluding the 4th subject). Bangla, English, Mathematics, Religion, ICT, and the three group subjects (Science / Commerce / Arts) are counted.

The 4th-subject rule

If your grade point in the 4th subject is greater than 2, the excess above 2 is added to your total grade points before averaging. Example: A+ in 4th subject = 5.00, so 5 − 2 = 3 bonus points added.

You can verify this calculation instantly using our SSC GPA Calculator.

HSC GPA — how it works

HSC (Higher Secondary Certificate) uses the same grading scale as SSC. The calculation rules are also the same — average of main subjects, plus bonus from the 4th subject if grade point exceeds 2.

The only difference: HSC has different group-specific main subjects. Science group includes Physics, Chemistry, Biology/Higher Math; Business Studies includes Accounting, Finance & Banking, Business Organisation; Humanities includes Economics, Civics, Logic, etc.

Use our HSC GPA Calculator to compute it with the 4th-subject bonus applied automatically.

University CGPA — how it works

Bangladeshi universities, following the UGC (University Grants Commission) standard, use a 4.00 scale, not 5.00. This is the single biggest source of confusion when students compare school and university grades.

UGC grading scale

Marks Letter Grade Grade Point
80–100 A+ 4.00
75–79 A 3.75
70–74 A− 3.50
65–69 B+ 3.25
60–64 B 3.00
55–59 B− 2.75
50–54 C+ 2.50
45–49 C 2.25
40–44 D 2.00
<40 F 0.00

The credit-weighted formula

Unlike SSC/HSC, university GPA is credit-weighted. Each course has a credit value (usually 3 or 4), and your GPA for a semester is:

Semester GPA = Σ (Grade Point × Credit) ÷ Σ Credits

Example:

Course Credits Grade GP GP × Credits
CSE101 3 A+ 4.00 12.00
MAT101 3 A 3.75 11.25
ENG101 3 B+ 3.25 9.75
PHY101 4 A− 3.50 14.00

Semester GPA = 47.00 ÷ 13 = 3.62

How CGPA is calculated

Cumulative GPA across all semesters uses the same formula — total quality points divided by total credits attempted. Our CGPA Calculator handles this automatically and includes a target-GPA planner.

Common confusion points

"My SSC GPA is 5.00, why is my university CGPA only 3.50?"

Different scales. SSC's 5.00 is roughly equivalent to UGC's 4.00. A 3.50 CGPA on the 4.00 scale is approximately 87.5% — equivalent to A+ at SSC.

"Why didn't the 4th subject apply at university?"

The 4th-subject bonus rule is unique to SSC and HSC. University courses are all credit-weighted; there is no equivalent.

"Some universities use a 4.00 scale; my university uses 4.00 too but the cutoffs are slightly different."

Most public and private universities in Bangladesh follow UGC's scale exactly, but a few (especially some private medical and engineering universities) use slightly different cutoffs. Always check your university's official grading sheet.

Converting Bangladesh CGPA to international scales

For study abroad, you'll often need to express your CGPA on a different scale:

  • US 4.0 scale: A Bangladesh 4.00 CGPA is roughly equivalent to a US 4.0 GPA. Most US universities accept WES evaluations as the authoritative conversion.
  • UK classification: CGPA 3.75+ ≈ First Class; 3.25–3.74 ≈ Upper Second (2:1); 2.75–3.24 ≈ Lower Second (2:2).
  • Percentage: Most universities issue a transcript with both CGPA and percentage. Don't try to convert one to the other yourself.

Related reading

  • CGPA to Percentage Conversion — Full Guide
  • How to Improve Your CGPA in 1 Semester
  • Complete Study Abroad Guide

FAQ

Is SSC GPA out of 5 or 4?
Out of 5.00 for all general boards in Bangladesh.

Is university CGPA out of 5 or 4?
Out of 4.00, following UGC guidelines.

Does the 4th subject count in SSC GPA?
Only the portion of its grade point that exceeds 2.00 is added as bonus to your total.

item.title: Top 10 Affordable Countries to Study Abroad for Bangladeshi Students
item.author: Study Koro
item.description: Ranked list of the cheapest study-abroad destinations for Bangladeshi students in 2026, covering tuition, living costs, scholarships, and work rights.
item.content:encoded:
Cost is usually the first real obstacle for Bangladeshi students who want to study abroad. Tuition is only part of it — visa fees, accommodation, food, transport, and health insurance can all add up quickly. The good news is that there are still plenty of countries where a serious student from Bangladesh can complete a quality degree without taking on crushing debt.

This guide ranks the ten most affordable study-abroad destinations for Bangladeshi students in 2026, based on average annual tuition, living costs, scholarship availability, and post-study work rights. Costs are rough averages — your real budget will depend on the city, the university, and your lifestyle.

1. Germany

Public universities in Germany charge no tuition for bachelor's and most master's programmes, even for international students. You only pay a semester contribution of roughly €150–350. Annual living cost in cities like Leipzig, Dresden, or Aachen is around €9,000–11,000. A blocked account of €11,904 is required for the student visa. German universities offer hundreds of English-taught master's programmes in engineering, computer science, and business.

2. Norway

Public universities in Norway were free for everyone until 2023, and remain free for EU/EEA students. International students now pay tuition, but it is still moderate (NOK 80,000–250,000 a year depending on the programme). Living costs are higher than Germany, but part-time work rights are generous.

3. Malaysia

Malaysia is one of the most popular budget destinations for Bangladeshi students. Tuition at private universities typically runs USD 3,000–6,000 a year, and many UK/Australian universities have branch campuses (Monash, Nottingham, Reading) where you get the same degree at a fraction of the cost. Living expenses in Kuala Lumpur are around USD 4,000–5,000 a year.

4. Hungary

The Hungarian government's Stipendium Hungaricum scholarship is one of the most accessible fully funded options for Bangladeshi students. It covers tuition, monthly stipend, accommodation, and medical insurance. Even self-funded, Hungary is cheap: tuition is around €1,500–5,000 a year and living costs in Budapest are around €6,000–8,000.

5. Poland

Poland has become a quiet favourite. Tuition for English-taught programmes is around €2,000–4,000 a year, and cities like Kraków, Wrocław, and Warsaw offer good infrastructure and a large international student community. Living costs are similar to Hungary.

6. China

The Chinese government, provinces, and individual universities offer a huge number of scholarships (CSC, Confucius, Belt & Road) for Bangladeshi students. Self-funded tuition is also cheap — RMB 18,000–35,000 a year. Living costs depend heavily on the city; tier-2 cities like Hefei or Wuhan are very affordable.

7. Russia

Russia offers the Open Doors and government scholarships, plus low-cost self-funded study (USD 2,500–6,000 a year). Medical universities in Russia are particularly popular for Bangladeshi students who couldn't get into BMDC-approved colleges at home, though you need to check the latest BMDC recognition list before committing.

8. Turkey

The Türkiye Bursları scholarship is fully funded and competitive. Self-funded tuition at Turkish state universities is around USD 500–1,500 a year. Istanbul and Ankara have lower living costs than most European cities.

9. India

India is geographically close, culturally familiar, and degrees from top Indian universities (IITs, IIMs, Delhi University, JNU) are well respected. The ICCR scholarship is offered specifically to Bangladeshi students. Self-funded tuition is moderate, and living costs are the lowest on this list.

10. Czech Republic

Czech public universities are free if you study in Czech. English-taught programmes cost around €4,000–8,000 a year. Prague offers excellent quality of life and Czech degrees are recognised across the EU.

How to choose between them

Don't pick a country based only on cost. Consider:

  • Language of instruction — English-taught programmes are easier short-term, but learning the local language unlocks part-time jobs and post-study work.
  • Post-study work rights — Germany gives 18 months, Malaysia 12, Hungary 9. China and Russia are stricter.
  • Field of study — engineering and IT are well represented everywhere; arts and humanities are stronger in Western Europe.
  • IELTS requirement — most of these countries accept IELTS 6.0–6.5. Check your target university's exact requirement and use our IELTS Band Score Calculator to plan your prep.

What to read next

  • How to Study Abroad from Bangladesh — Complete Guide
  • How to Write a Statement of Purpose (SOP) — With Examples
  • Student Visa Interview: Common Questions and How to Answer

FAQ

Which is the cheapest country to study abroad for Bangladeshi students?
Germany is the cheapest overall because public-university tuition is free. Hungary, Poland, and Malaysia are close behind if you include scholarships.

Can I work part-time while studying in these countries?
Yes — most of them allow 20 hours per week during term and full-time during holidays. Earnings depend heavily on the local minimum wage.

Do I need IELTS for all of them?
Almost always. A few universities accept MOI (Medium of Instruction) certificates from Bangladeshi institutions, but IELTS 6.0–6.5 is the safest baseline.

item.title: Study Tour Application: Format, Tips, and 5 Examples for Students
item.author: Study Koro
item.description: Learn how to write a study tour application with the correct format. Includes 5 examples for school and college students plus simple writing tips.
item.content:encoded:
A study tour is an exciting part of student life. It allows students to visit historical places, industries, museums, universities, and different cities. Through these trips, students learn outside the classroom and gain real world knowledge.

However, before joining a tour, students usually need to submit a study tour application to their teacher, principal, or department head. This application asks for permission to participate in the tour.

In this guide, you will learn what a study tour application is, why schools require it, the proper format, useful writing tips, and several examples you can use as templates.

What Is a Study Tour Application?

A study tour application is a formal letter written by a student requesting permission to join an educational trip organized by a school, college, or university.

The application usually includes:

  • Student information
  • Purpose of the tour
  • Destination
  • Duration of the tour
  • A polite request for permission

Educational tours may include visits to museums, cultural places, industries, or universities. For example, students often visit famous educational locations such as the National Museum of Bangladesh or historical places like the Lalbagh Fort to learn about culture and history.

Because these tours involve travel and responsibility, institutions require formal permission requests.

Why Schools Require a Study Tour Application

Schools and colleges request applications for several important reasons.

1. Official Permission

The application allows teachers or principals to officially approve your participation in the tour.

2. Student Records

Institutions maintain records of students who are attending the trip.

3. Safety and Responsibility

If something unexpected happens during the tour, the school has documentation that the student received official permission.

4. Organization

Applications help schools manage the number of participants and make better arrangements for transportation and accommodation.

Format of a Study Tour Application

Writing a proper application is simple when you follow the correct structure.

1. Receiver Information

Start by addressing the person responsible for approving the tour.

Example:

To The Principal / Head Teacher School or College Name

2. Subject Line

Clearly mention the purpose of the letter.

Example:

Subject: Application for permission to join the study tour

3. Salutation

Use a polite greeting.

Example:

Respected Sir/Madam,

4. Body Paragraph

Explain your request clearly.

Include:

  • Tour destination
  • Tour date
  • Educational purpose

5. Closing

End with a polite request and gratitude.

Example:

I kindly request you to grant me permission to participate in the study tour.

6. Signature

Finish with your details.

Example:

  • Your name
  • Class or department
  • Roll number
  • Date

Example 1: Study Tour Application for School Students

To The Principal ABC High School

Subject: Application for permission to join the study tour

Respected Sir,

I respectfully state that our school is organizing a study tour to the National Museum next week. The tour will help students learn more about the history and culture of our country.

I am very interested in joining this educational trip with my classmates. It will provide valuable learning experience outside the classroom.

Therefore, I kindly request you to grant me permission to participate in the study tour.

Thank you for your consideration.

Yours obediently Raihan Class: 9 Roll: 12 Date: 16 March 2026

Example 2: Study Tour Application for College Students

To The Principal XYZ College

Subject: Application for permission to go on a study tour

Respected Sir,

With due respect, I would like to inform you that our department has arranged a study tour to a historical site next month. The purpose of this tour is to help students gain practical knowledge related to our academic subjects.

I would like to join this tour along with my classmates. I believe the trip will enhance our understanding and provide valuable educational exposure.

Therefore, I kindly request you to allow me to participate in the study tour.

Yours faithfully Raihan Ahmed Department: History Roll: 24 Date: 16 March 2026

Example 3: Short Study Tour Application

To The Head Teacher ABC School

Subject: Permission for study tour

Respected Sir,

Our school is planning a study tour next week. I would like to participate in this educational trip with my classmates.

I kindly request you to grant me permission to join the study tour.

Thank you.

Yours obediently Raihan Class 10 Roll 5

Example 4: Application from Parents

Sometimes schools require permission from parents.

To The Principal ABC High School

Subject: Permission for my son to join the study tour

Respected Sir,

I am the father of Raihan, a student of class nine in your school. I have learned that the school is organizing a study tour next week.

I am happy to allow my son to participate in this educational trip. I believe it will be a great learning opportunity for him.

Thank you for organizing such activities for students.

Sincerely Mr. Karim Parent of Raihan

Example 5: Application for University Study Tour

To The Head of Department Department of Geography XYZ University

Subject: Request for permission to participate in study tour

Respected Sir,

Our department is arranging a study tour as part of the academic program. I am very interested in joining the trip because it will help me understand practical aspects of our course.

I believe the tour will improve our knowledge and provide valuable field experience.

Therefore, I request you to kindly grant me permission to participate in the study tour.

Yours sincerely Raihan Ahmed Department of Geography Student ID: 20345

Tips for Writing a Good Study Tour Application

Follow these tips to write a strong application.

Keep the Language Simple

Use clear and easy sentences so the reader quickly understands your request.

Be Polite

Always maintain a respectful tone when addressing teachers or principals.

Stay Short and Clear

An application should be brief. Avoid unnecessary details.

Include Important Information

Mention:

  • destination
  • purpose
  • date (if known)

Check Grammar

Before submitting, review your application for spelling and grammar mistakes.

Final Thoughts

Study tours are an excellent way for students to learn beyond textbooks. Visiting educational places, museums, and cultural sites helps students gain practical knowledge and new experiences.

Writing a proper study tour application ensures that you receive official permission from your school or college. By following the correct format and maintaining a polite tone, you can easily write an effective application.

You can also use the examples in this guide as templates and adjust them according to your school or college requirements.

item.title: How to Study Abroad from Bangladesh — Complete Guide 2026
item.author: Study Koro
item.description: Everything a Bangladeshi student needs to know: choosing a country, IELTS requirements, scholarships, the visa process, and what to expect when you arrive.
item.content:encoded:
Every year, tens of thousands of Bangladeshi students leave for universities in the UK, Australia, Canada, the United States, Germany, Malaysia, and beyond. Studying abroad opens doors to world-class education, international work experience, and often a pathway to residency in a new country. But the process — from choosing a university to landing at the airport with a student visa in hand — can feel overwhelming if you don't know where to start.

This guide walks you through every stage of the journey, step by step, with specific information relevant to students from Bangladesh.

Why Study Abroad from Bangladesh?

Bangladesh has made enormous strides in its domestic university sector, but studying at a recognized international institution still carries significant advantages for Bangladeshi students:

  • Global degree recognition — Degrees from UK, Australian, Canadian, and American universities are accepted by employers worldwide without question.
  • Post-study work rights — The UK's Graduate Route visa (2 years), Australia's Temporary Graduate visa (2–4 years), and Canada's Post-Graduation Work Permit (up to 3 years) let you gain international work experience after graduating.
  • Pathways to residency — Canada and Australia in particular have structured immigration systems where studying locally can significantly strengthen a permanent residency application.
  • Research and facilities — Access to research labs, libraries, and academic networks that are simply unavailable in Bangladesh for most fields.
  • Personal growth — Language fluency, cultural adaptability, and independence are qualities that employers across every industry increasingly value.

Step-by-Step: How to Study Abroad from Bangladesh

1

Decide What You Want to Study and Why

Before choosing a country or university, be clear on your field, level (undergraduate or postgraduate), and career goal. Different countries have different strengths — engineering in Germany, business in the UK, healthcare in Australia, technology in Canada. Your choice of field should drive your choice of destination.

2

Check Your Academic Eligibility

Most undergraduate programs abroad require your SSC and HSC results. A GPA of 4.00+ in HSC (out of 5.00) is generally competitive. For postgraduate programs, your bachelor's degree transcript is the key document — a CGPA of 3.00+ (out of 4.00) from a recognized Bangladesh university is typically the minimum. Use our HSC GPA Calculator and CGPA Calculator to verify your scores.

3

Take IELTS (or an Accepted Alternative)

For English-medium programs in the UK, Australia, Canada, and USA, an English language test is mandatory. IELTS Academic is the most widely accepted. Aim for at least 6.5 overall for most universities. See the IELTS requirements section below for country-by-country details.

4

Research Universities and Programs

Use official university websites, QS World University Rankings, and the Times Higher Education rankings. Apply to a range of universities — 2–3 reach schools, 3–4 target schools, and 2 safe options. Pay attention to entry requirements, tuition fees, and scholarship availability for international students.

5

Apply for Scholarships Early

Scholarships have earlier deadlines than university applications — sometimes by 3–6 months. Research government scholarships (Chevening, Australia Awards, Commonwealth) and university merit scholarships simultaneously with your applications.

6

Submit University Applications

Prepare your Statement of Purpose (SOP), academic transcripts, recommendation letters (usually 2–3), CV, and proof of English proficiency. Deadlines vary — UK universities via UCAS typically close in January for September intake; Australian and Canadian universities often have rolling admissions.

7

Apply for Your Student Visa

Once you have a Conditional or Unconditional Offer and have accepted it, you can apply for a student visa. You will need proof of funds (typically covering 1 year of tuition + living costs), your offer letter, IELTS results, and passport photos. Apply at least 3 months before your course start date.

8

Prepare to Depart

Arrange student accommodation (university halls or private), open a student bank account in your destination country (many banks let you do this online before arriving), sort travel and health insurance, and attend any pre-departure orientation offered by your university or the Bangladesh embassy.

IELTS Score Requirements by Country

The IELTS Academic test is required for admission to most English-medium programs abroad. Here are the typical minimum requirements by destination country. Note that individual programs may require higher scores.

Country Undergraduate Minimum Postgraduate Minimum No Band Below
🇬🇧 United Kingdom 6.0 overall 6.5 overall 5.5
🇦🇺 Australia 6.0–6.5 overall 6.5 overall 6.0
🇨🇦 Canada 6.0–6.5 overall 6.5–7.0 overall 6.0
🇺🇸 United States 6.5 overall 7.0 overall 6.0
🇩🇪 Germany 6.0 (English programs) 6.5 (English programs) 5.5
🇲🇾 Malaysia 5.5–6.0 overall 6.0–6.5 overall 5.0
🇳🇿 New Zealand 6.0 overall 6.5 overall 5.5

💡 Tip

Use our free IELTS Band Score Calculator to estimate your overall band from your section scores. Aim to score at least 0.5 above the minimum requirement to give yourself a buffer.

Choosing the Right Country

United Kingdom

The UK remains one of the most popular destinations for Bangladeshi students. Undergraduate degrees take 3 years (saving one year vs Bangladesh or the US), and the Graduate Route visa allows 2 years of post-study work after graduation (3 years for PhD graduates). Tuition fees range from £10,000 to £38,000 per year. Living costs in London are significantly higher than other cities — consider universities in Manchester, Birmingham, Leeds, or Sheffield for better value.

Australia

Australia offers a high quality of life and strong student work rights — you can work up to 48 hours per fortnight while studying. The Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485) allows 2–4 years of work rights after graduation, depending on the qualification and state where you study. Tuition fees range from AUD 20,000 to AUD 45,000 per year. Sydney and Melbourne are expensive; consider Brisbane, Adelaide, or Perth.

Canada

Canada has one of the clearest pathways from student to permanent resident. The Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP) allows up to 3 years of work after completing a degree of 2+ years. Points earned from a Canadian degree and work experience can be used in the Express Entry immigration system. Tuition varies widely — CAD 15,000 to CAD 35,000 per year for international students.

Germany

Public universities in Germany charge little to no tuition fees for international students — you typically pay only a semester fee of €150–400. The catch is that most programs at the bachelor's level are taught in German. However, Germany has a rapidly growing number of English-taught master's programs, particularly in engineering, computer science, and business. Living costs are moderate at approximately €800–1,100 per month.

Malaysia

Malaysia is an increasingly popular and affordable alternative for Bangladeshi students. Tuition fees are significantly lower (MYR 15,000–60,000 per year), the cost of living is manageable, and many universities offer programs taught in English. It is also geographically and culturally closer to Bangladesh, making it easier for students who haven't studied or lived far from home before.

Cost of Studying Abroad from Bangladesh

Country Tuition (per year) Living Costs (per month) Work Rights
UK £10,000–£38,000 £800–£1,500 20 hrs/week term-time
Australia AUD 20,000–45,000 AUD 1,500–2,500 48 hrs/fortnight
Canada CAD 15,000–35,000 CAD 1,200–2,000 20 hrs/week off-campus
Germany €0–500 (public) €800–1,100 120 full days/year
Malaysia MYR 15,000–60,000 MYR 1,500–2,500 20 hrs/week (approved jobs)

ℹ️ Note

Exchange rates fluctuate significantly against the Bangladeshi Taka. Always budget with a 10–15% buffer and monitor rates using a reliable financial app before sending money abroad.

Scholarships for Bangladeshi Students

Funding your education abroad is the biggest challenge most Bangladeshi families face. The good news: there are dozens of scholarships specifically open to Bangladeshi students.

Government-Funded Scholarships

  • Chevening Scholarship (UK) — Fully funded by the UK government for outstanding future leaders. Covers tuition, living allowance, flights, and visa. For postgraduate study only. Deadline is typically November each year.
  • Australia Awards Scholarship — Fully funded by the Australian government for students from developing countries. Covers tuition, travel, Overseas Student Health Cover, and a living allowance. Very competitive — apply 12–18 months in advance.
  • Commonwealth Scholarship — For students from Commonwealth countries including Bangladesh. Covers full study costs for master's and PhD programs at UK universities.
  • DAAD Scholarship (Germany) — The German Academic Exchange Service offers numerous scholarships for Bangladeshi students for study and research in Germany. Many cover tuition, health insurance, and a monthly stipend of around €850–1,200.
  • Erasmus+ Scholarship (Europe) — Supports study or traineeships at European universities. Bangladesh students at eligible partner universities can apply.
  • China Government Scholarship (CSC) — Fully funded scholarships for undergraduate, master's, and PhD study at Chinese universities. No tuition fees, free accommodation, health insurance, and a monthly stipend.

University Merit Scholarships

Most universities in the UK, Australia, and Canada offer merit-based scholarships or fee reductions for high-achieving international students. These range from 10% to 100% of tuition. Check each university's international scholarships page — deadlines are usually the same as or shortly after the application deadline.

💡 Tip

Apply for scholarships and universities simultaneously. Many scholarship applications require a university offer letter, so begin both processes at the same time rather than waiting for admission before starting your scholarship search.

Documents You Will Need

  • Valid passport — At least 18 months validity beyond your course end date
  • SSC and HSC transcripts and certificates — Attested by the Bangladesh education board
  • Bachelor's degree transcript and provisional certificate (for postgraduate applicants)
  • IELTS Academic result — Original TRF (Test Report Form), usually valid for 2 years
  • Statement of Purpose (SOP) — 500–1,000 words explaining why you want to study this program
  • 2–3 Reference Letters — From academic supervisors or professors who know your work
  • CV/Resume — Academic and extracurricular achievements
  • Bank statement — Showing sufficient funds (usually 12 months of tuition + living costs)
  • Passport-size photographs — Requirements vary by country
  • Health insurance / OSHC — Required before visa issuance in Australia

Frequently Asked Questions

What IELTS score do I need to study abroad from Bangladesh?

Most programs in the UK, Australia, and Canada require 6.0–6.5 overall for undergraduate and 6.5–7.0 for postgraduate. No individual band should fall below 5.5 in most cases. Use our IELTS calculator to check your estimated score.

How much money do I need to show in my bank for a student visa?

Requirements vary by country. For a UK Student visa, you typically need to show funds covering 9 months of tuition + £1,334/month living costs (outside London) or £1,023/month (in London). For Australia, you need to show AUD 21,041 per year for living expenses, plus your full tuition. For Canada, you need CAD 10,000 per year above tuition. These figures are updated periodically — check the official embassy website before applying.

Can I study abroad from Bangladesh without IELTS?

Some universities accept TOEFL, PTE Academic, or Duolingo English Test as alternatives. Germany, Japan, and China offer programs in languages other than English. A few UK universities also waive IELTS if your previous education was conducted entirely in English — check individual institution policies.

Which country is easiest for Bangladeshi students to get a student visa?

Malaysia and Germany have relatively straightforward student visa processes for Bangladeshi nationals. The UK and Australia are more rigorous but manageable with proper documentation. Canada has become stricter in recent years; ensure your financial documents are clear and your study permit application is complete.

Can I work while studying abroad?

Yes, in most countries. The UK allows 20 hours/week during term time. Australia allows 48 hours per fortnight. Canada allows 20 hours/week off-campus. Germany allows 120 full working days per year. Always check the specific conditions of your visa — working beyond permitted hours can jeopardize your visa status.

item.title: IELTS Preparation Tips for Bangladeshi Students — Band 7+ Strategy
item.author: Study Koro
item.description: A section-by-section breakdown of the IELTS test and a concrete, actionable preparation strategy for students in Bangladesh.
item.content:encoded:
IELTS is the gateway to studying, working, or migrating abroad for most Bangladeshi students. Yet many students sit the test two, three, or even four times before reaching their target — not because they lack the English ability, but because they don't understand what the test is actually measuring and how to prepare for it systematically.

This guide breaks down the IELTS test section by section and gives you a concrete, actionable preparation strategy. Whether you're targeting Band 6.0 for a conditional university offer or Band 7.5+ for a competitive scholarship, the approach is the same — it's the depth and duration of preparation that differs.

First: Understand What IELTS Actually Tests

IELTS does not test how much vocabulary you know or how many grammar rules you've memorized. It tests your ability to use English naturally and accurately in real-world contexts. This distinction matters enormously for how you prepare.

The four sections test:

  • Listening — Following spoken English at natural speed, in different accents (British, Australian, American, Canadian), with a single play.
  • Reading — Locating and interpreting information in long, complex texts under significant time pressure.
  • Writing — Producing structured, formal written English in two distinct task formats.
  • Speaking — Conducting a natural, extended conversation in English with a real examiner.

The overall band is the average of all four, rounded using the official .25/.75 rule. Use our IELTS Band Score Calculator to estimate your overall band from your section scores.

What Band Score Do You Need?

Goal Minimum Overall Band No Band Below
UK university undergraduate 6.0 5.5
UK university postgraduate 6.5 6.0
Australian university 6.5 6.0
Canadian university 6.5 6.0
Chevening Scholarship 6.5 6.0
Australia Awards Scholarship 6.5 6.0
UK Graduate Route visa No IELTS required post-study —
Australian skilled migration 6.0 (10 pts) / 7.0 (20 pts) 6.0 / 7.0

Section-by-Section Preparation

🎧

Listening — Target: 30–35 correct (Band 7.0–8.0)

40 questions · 30 minutes + 10 minutes transfer time

The Listening section plays once — you cannot rewind. Speakers use British, Australian, North American, and New Zealand accents. Bangladeshi students who have primarily learned English from local teachers often struggle with unfamiliar accents, particularly Australian and Scottish.

  • Listen to BBC World Service, ABC Australia, and CBC Canada podcasts daily for at least 30 minutes. Exposure to natural, varied accents is the single biggest lever.
  • Practice reading questions before the audio begins. You get 30–45 seconds before each section — use it to predict what information you need.
  • Write exactly what you hear. The answer is almost always the exact word spoken — don't paraphrase. Check spelling carefully.
  • Sections 3 and 4 (academic discussion, lecture) are harder than Sections 1 and 2. Practice these specifically.
  • Complete at least 10 full timed Listening tests from Cambridge IELTS books. Review every wrong answer to understand why you missed it.

📖

Reading — Target: 30–35 correct (Band 7.0–8.0)

40 questions · 60 minutes · 3 long passages

The Reading section is primarily a time management challenge. Most students can find the answers — they simply run out of time. 60 minutes for 40 questions across three dense academic texts means roughly 20 minutes per passage.

  • Do NOT read the entire passage first. Read the questions, then skim-read to find the relevant section, then read that part carefully.
  • True/False/Not Given and Yes/No/Not Given questions are the most commonly missed. "Not Given" means the text doesn't mention the statement at all — not that it contradicts it.
  • For Matching Headings questions, read the first and last sentence of each paragraph first. Headings summarize the main idea, not specific details.
  • Read one quality English article every day from The Guardian, The Economist, or BBC News. This builds vocabulary in context.
  • Academic Reading is harder than General Training Reading for the same band score. If you're doing Academic, practice with Academic materials only.

✍️

Writing — Target: Band 7.0

Task 1 (150 words) + Task 2 (250 words) · 60 minutes total

Writing is the section where Bangladeshi students most often fall short of their target. The problem is almost never grammar — it's task response and coherence. Examiners are checking whether you answered the question directly, organized your argument logically, and used a range of vocabulary and grammar structures accurately.

  • Spend 20 minutes on Task 1 and 40 minutes on Task 2. Task 2 is worth twice as many marks — always prioritize it.
  • Task 1 Academic requires you to describe data objectively — no personal opinion. Describe the most significant trends, not every detail.
  • Task 2 requires a clear position in your introduction, two or three developed body paragraphs, and a conclusion. Never write a list of ideas without developing them.
  • Get your essays marked by a certified IELTS examiner or a qualified tutor who gives band-specific feedback. Practicing writing without feedback is significantly less effective.
  • Avoid repeating the same words. Use synonyms, but only ones you're confident about — incorrect word choice hurts more than repetition.

🗣️

Speaking — Target: Band 7.0

11–14 minutes · 3 parts · face-to-face with examiner

Speaking is often the lowest-scoring section for Bangladeshi students — not because of language ability, but because of hesitation, short answers, and anxiety. The examiner is not looking for perfect accuracy; they are looking for fluency, range of vocabulary, and the ability to develop ideas spontaneously.

  • Practice speaking for 1–2 minutes on any given topic without stopping. Set a timer. Common Part 2 topics include: describe a place, describe a person who influenced you, describe a memorable experience.
  • In Part 3, give extended answers. Use the structure: Opinion → Reason → Example → Restate. Aim for 4–6 sentences per answer.
  • Record yourself speaking and listen back. This is uncomfortable but it is the fastest way to identify filler words, pronunciation issues, and unnatural pauses.
  • Do not memorize answers. Examiners are trained to identify scripted responses and will ask follow-up questions that break your memorized script.
  • Speak with a language partner daily — even 15 minutes of unscripted English conversation is enormously valuable.

12-Week IELTS Study Plan

This plan assumes you can dedicate 1.5–2 hours per day. Adjust duration if targeting a higher band or starting from a lower base.

Weeks 1–2

Diagnostic & Foundation

Take a full timed mock test under exam conditions to establish your baseline band. Identify your two weakest sections. Study official IELTS band descriptors for each skill. Begin daily English reading (The Guardian, BBC News) and listening (BBC Podcasts).

Weeks 3–5

Targeted Skill Practice

Focus intensively on your two weakest sections. Complete one timed Listening or Reading practice daily. Write two Task 2 essays per week and get them marked. Practice speaking for 15 minutes daily with a partner or by recording yourself.

Weeks 6–8

Full Section Drills

Complete full timed Listening tests 3× per week and full Reading tests 3× per week. Write one Task 1 and one Task 2 per week. Expand vocabulary with IELTS word lists. Do 2–3 mock Speaking tests with a tutor or language partner.

Weeks 9–11

Full Mock Tests & Refinement

Take a full timed mock test every 5–6 days. Review every wrong answer thoroughly. Focus on question types that still cause errors. Continue daily listening and reading habits. Polish Speaking with special attention to Part 2 fluency.

Week 12

Final Preparation

No new materials. Review your most common errors from the past 11 weeks. One final mock test on Day 7 of this week. Rest 2 days before your test. Prepare your ID, know your test centre location, and sleep well the night before.

💡 Resource Recommendation

Use Cambridge IELTS books 14–19 (the most recent) for authentic practice tests. The British Council's official IELTS website offers free sample tests. For Writing feedback, use a certified IELTS examiner — free online services rarely provide band-accurate feedback.

Common Mistakes Bangladeshi Students Make

❌ Mistake 1

Memorizing vocabulary lists without learning words in context. Knowing that "ubiquitous" means "everywhere" is not the same as being able to use it correctly in a sentence.

✓ Fix

Read quality English articles daily. When you encounter an unfamiliar word, note the sentence around it — not just the definition.

❌ Mistake 2

Writing Task 2 essays without a clear position. Many Bangladeshi students write "on one hand... on the other hand..." without ever stating what they actually think.

✓ Fix

State your position clearly in the introduction: "I believe that..." or "This essay argues that..." Then spend the body paragraphs supporting that position with reasons and examples.

❌ Mistake 3

Giving one-word or one-sentence answers in the Speaking test. Examiners need to hear you sustain English for extended periods — short answers give them nothing to evaluate.

✓ Fix

Treat every Speaking question as a mini-essay. Expand with reasons, examples, and contrasts. If you finish after 30 seconds, add "However, I also think that..." or "For example..."

❌ Mistake 4

Spending too long on hard Listening or Reading questions. Spending 3 minutes on question 8 means you miss questions 9–12 entirely.

✓ Fix

Move on after 30–45 seconds on any question you're unsure about. Mark it and return if time allows. A guess is always better than a blank.

❌ Mistake 5

Preparing only with non-official materials or YouTube shortcuts. The question formats, timing, and difficulty in unofficial materials often don't match the real test.

✓ Fix

Base your preparation on official Cambridge IELTS books and the British Council/IDP practice platforms. Use unofficial materials only to supplement, not replace, official practice.

Frequently Asked Questions

How long does it take to prepare for IELTS from Bangladesh?

Students targeting Band 6.0–6.5 typically need 6–8 weeks of focused preparation. Those targeting Band 7.0+ often need 3–6 months. The key variable is your current English level — the further you are from your target, the longer the preparation required.

Is IELTS Academic harder than General Training?

Yes, particularly in Reading. Academic Reading uses more complex texts and requires more answers correct to achieve the same band. If you are applying for university programs, you must take Academic IELTS regardless — General Training is for migration and non-academic purposes.

Where can I take IELTS in Bangladesh?

IELTS is available at multiple centres in Dhaka, including the British Council (Dhaka) and IDP Bangladesh (Dhaka, Chittagong, Sylhet). Tests are offered multiple times per month. Book as early as possible — popular dates fill up 6–8 weeks in advance.

How many times can I take IELTS?

There is no limit. IELTS results are valid for 2 years. Many students take the test 2–3 times before achieving their target. Each attempt gives you valuable information about which sections to focus on.

Should I take IELTS on computer or paper?

Both formats test the same content and award the same scores. Computer-delivered IELTS has the advantage of faster results (usually 3–5 days vs 13 days for paper). The Writing and Speaking sections are identical in both formats — if you type faster than you write, computer IELTS may suit you better.
